Part 1 · Chemical foundations

Why Chemistry Matters in Biology

Understanding biomolecules allows us to…

🔬

Explain life

Cellular structure, metabolism and heredity are chemical processes.

💊

Fight disease

Understand disease, improve diagnosis and design new drugs.

🩺

Practise medicine

Biomedical sciences depend on interpreting chemical interactions in the body.

🧪 Example: a blood-glucose test, a cholesterol panel and an insulin injection are all chemistry applied to a patient — we'll meet all three today.

➡️ The molecule has a dipole moment — it is polar.

Why is water polar?

Electronegativity: a tug-of-war for electrons

O = 3.44

Oxygen: high electronegativity — strong pull on electrons.

H = 2.20

Hydrogen: lower electronegativity.

Shared electrons spend more time near O → O is δ−, each H is δ+.

Two sticky behaviours

Cohesion & Adhesion

🤝 Cohesion

Water molecules stick to each other — due to hydrogen bonding.

Surface molecules have fewer neighbours, so they bond more strongly to the ones they have → surface tension → spherical droplets.

🧲 Adhesion

Water sticks to other polar or charged surfaces — also via hydrogen bonds.

🤔 THINK · PAIR · SHARE

How do insects walk on water's surface?

Discuss with your neighbour for 60 seconds, then press → to reveal.

🦟 The water strider spreads its weight on long legs; cohesion creates surface tension — a “skin” that resists breaking.

🌳 Cohesion + adhesion also move water to the tops of trees and drain tears from your tear ducts. A carefully placed needle can even float on water!

Scientific comparison

Cohesion vs Adhesion

CohesionAdhesion
DefinitionAttraction between water moleculesAttraction between water and other surfaces
Caused byHydrogen bonding among water moleculesH-bonding or electrostatic interaction with other materials
ExamplesSurface tension, dropletsCapillary action
Biological roleMaintains the water column in plantsHelps water climb plant vessels; hydrates tissues
🩸

Clinical: cohesion helps maintain blood plasma integrity and fluid stability in capillaries.

🧫

Clinical: adhesion lets water interact with cell components — enzyme function, membrane hydration, molecular transport.

Part 2

The Four Biomolecules of Life

Building big molecules

Polymerization

A monomer is a building block; many monomers join to form a polymer.

➕ Dehydration synthesis: monomers join and a molecule of H₂O is released.

✂️ Hydrolysis: water is added to break the bond (this is what digestion does).

Biomolecule 1

Carbohydrates

⚡ The main energy source for living organisms.

Made of C, H and O in a ratio of 1 : 2 : 1 → general formula (CH₂O)ₙ.

C ×1
H ×2
O ×1

🔗 Sugar units are joined by glycosidic linkages (e.g. the β-1,4 bond in lactose).

Types of carbohydrates · 1

Monosaccharides — single sugars

A single sugar molecule with a backbone of 3–7 carbons.

Pentoses (5 C): ribose, deoxyribose
Hexoses (6 C): glucose, fructose, galactose

In our body, the hexose glucose is the most common and the immediate source of energy.

🧪 BUILD A DISACCHARIDE

Two monosaccharides → one disaccharide

Pick two sugars and join them by a dehydration reaction.

Sugar 1

Types of carbohydrates · 3

Polysaccharides — long glucose polymers

🥔 Starch

Energy store in plants (e.g. potato roots). Helical, slightly branched.

🍖 Glycogen

Energy store in animals (liver & muscle). Highly branched → fast release.

🌿 Cellulose

Structural — plant cell walls. Straight chains H-bonded into fibres.

Biomolecule 2

Lipids

Made of C, H and O (some also contain P and N) — far fewer O atoms than carbohydrates.

💧❌ They do not dissolve in water — mostly non-polar.

🔗 Fats form by joining glycerol + 3 fatty acids through ester bonds.

📌 Note: lipids are not true polymers — fatty acids don't repeat in long chains the way glucose does in starch.

⚡ QUICK CHECK · SORT IT

Water-loving or water-fearing?

Hydrophilic: polar / charged · forms H-bonds with water · dissolves easily.

Hydrophobic: non-polar · no H-bonds with water · water pushes them together (hydrophobic interaction).

Types of lipids

Three families, three jobs

⚡ Fat stores ~9 kcal/g — more than twice carbohydrates (~4 kcal/g). That's why adipose tissue is the body's long-term energy reserve.

🩺 CLINICAL SIMULATION

LDL, HDL & atherosclerosis

LDL (“bad”) level: 100 mg/dL

HDL (“good”) level: 55 mg/dL

Artery opening

100%

LDL carries cholesterol from the liver to tissues; excess sticks to artery walls → plaque → heart attack & stroke risk.

HDL collects extra cholesterol and returns it to the liver.

Also linked to lipids: fatty liver disease and membrane / lipid-raft disorders.

Wrap-up

Summary of Key Concepts

💧 Water is polar (bent, 104.5°) and forms hydrogen bonds.

🔗 H-bonds give cohesion, adhesion, high heat capacity, solvent power and floating ice.

🍞 Carbohydrates: mono-, di-, polysaccharides; energy & structure; insulin controls blood glucose.

🧈 Lipids: hydrophobic; energy storage, membranes (phospholipid bilayer), hormones; LDL/HDL in heart disease.
